problem: VLN agents overfit to dataset biases, such as familiar visual layouts and decoration styles, frequent instruction keywords, sentence patterns and trajectory trends, so they generalize poorly to unseen environments. Prior remedies mostly collect or synthesize more data or add more input types (objects, depth, graphs), and do not debias the model itself.
motivation: A perfectly unbiased VLN dataset is practically unattainable, which leads to a cycle of 'create dataset, find bias, create new dataset'. The authors want to move from diagnosis to treatment with a model that learns cause-effect relations instead of spurious correlations. The observation driving the paper is that confounders influence both the inputs (vision, language, history) and the actions. Some confounders are observable (room types, direction/landmark keywords) and others are not (style, sentence patterns, trajectory trends). A toy statistic on R2R train shows that P(Y|do(X)) differs from P(Y|X) for keywords such as 'table' and 'stairs'.
key_idea: Model VLN with a structural causal model that has observable and unobservable confounders, and apply do-operator interventions at the feature level: back-door adjustment with explicit confounder dictionaries (keywords, rooms) and front-door adjustment with K-means-sampled global feature dictionaries (vision, language, history) built by a contrastively trained cross-modal pooling module.
insight: The two adjustments are complementary. On R2R val-unseen, BACL alone raises SPL from 64.69 to 67.13 and FACL alone to 66.92; together they reach 68.13 (SR 75.27→77.82). This supports the claim that both observable and unobservable confounders matter. Details of the intervention also matter. Intervening on intermediate features beats intervening only before the final softmax (SPL 68.13 vs 66.80). Updating confounder dictionaries during training helps (66.20 without). Attention-based expectation works best for text and statistic (frequency-weighted) expectation for vision; the paper attributes this to RoBERTa being trained end-to-end while CLIP is frozen. A caveat for readers: the no-intervention baseline already gets SR 75.27 / SPL 64.69 on R2R val-unseen, which is on par with or above BEVBert (75/64). Much of the headline gain over SOTA therefore comes from the strong base setup (CLIP-B/16, METER init, augmented data, EnvEdit, speaker pseudo-labels), not from causal learning alone.
method: Structural causal model: inputs X = {vision V, instruction I, history H} and output Y = action. Confounders are split into observable ones (room references z_v^o, direction/landmark keywords z_i^o) and unobservable ones (visual style, sentence pattern, trajectory trend); mediators M are inserted for the front-door path.

BACL (back-door adjustment causal learning): implements the adjustment at the feature level as f_x(x)+E_z[f_z(z)] over a confounder dictionary. The text dictionary has 74 direction/landmark keyword classes, found by POS tags and averaged from RoBERTa features, and is updated end-to-end with attention-based expectation. The vision dictionary has 50 room types, labelled by querying BLIP VQA with 'what kind of room is this?' on CLIP features, and uses statistic (frequency-weighted) expectation. Outputs are fused via FC+LN before a 2-layer panorama transformer.

FACL (front-door adjustment causal learning): approximates E_x'[x'] + E_{m|x}[m] with two query embeddings over (a) cross-sampled global features x' drawn from K-means clusters (24 clusters) of the whole training set and (b) in-sample features m. Implemented with multi-head attention and applied separately to the vision, history and text sequences.

Adaptive gate fusion (AGF): a sigmoid gate mixes the causality-enhanced features R_x with the original context features G_x per modality. METER-style cross-attention encoders then produce local (vision-text) and global (history/graph-text) features, which are dynamically fused as in DUET for action prediction.

CFP (cross-modal feature pooling): one transformer layer followed by tanh attentive pooling compresses the vision, history, fused and text sequences into single vectors. It is trained in pre-training with CLIP-style symmetric contrastive losses (local-text, global-text, fused-text) alongside MLM/SAP (plus OG for REVERIE/SOON). In fine-tuning it extracts the global features that are K-means clustered into front-door dictionaries.

Training: DUET-style dual-scale graph transformer (6 text, 2 panorama, 3 cross-modal layers) initialized from METER. Pre-training runs up to 300K iterations (batch 48, lr 5e-5) on synthetic augmented data plus EnvEdit features. Fine-tuning runs up to 100K iterations (lr 2e-5) with cross-entropy and speaker-generated pseudo-labels with environmental dropout; dictionaries are refreshed periodically.

setting.backbone: DUET-style dual-scale graph transformer initialized from METER, with an end-to-end-trained RoBERTa text encoder and frozen CLIP-B/16 image features (trained/fine-tuned)
setting.training_data: R2R / RxR-English / REVERIE / SOON training sets plus synthetic augmented instruction data in pre-training (PREVALENT-style augmentation for R2R, augmented data from wang2023res for REVERIE, wang2022less for RxR). EnvEdit style-transferred features are used for augmentation. Speaker models with environmental dropout give dynamic pseudo-labels in fine-tuning. BLIP (VQA) is used offline to label room types for the visual confounder dictionary.
setting.observation: panoramic RGB (36 views, CLIP-B/16 features) with heading/elevation; plus object features for REVERIE/SOON
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph viewpoints (select node from global topological graph or STOP)
setting.privileged: none (standard discrete nav-graph setting; REVERIE/SOON use provided object annotations as candidates)

numbers_note: The multi-dataset 'w/o intervention' ablation (Fig. 6), the K-means cluster-number sweep, and the GFLOPs vs accuracy comparison appear only in figures without printed numbers. RxR results cover only the English subset and only the val splits (no test). REVERIE RGS is reported but SOON reports RGSPL only (no RGS).
results: GOAT sets a new state of the art on four discrete VLN benchmarks. On R2R test-unseen it reaches SR 74.57 / SPL 64.94 vs BEVBert 73/62, and SR 77.82 / SPL 68.13 on val-unseen. On REVERIE test-unseen it gets SR 57.72 / RGSPL 26.70 vs DSRG 54.04 / GridMM 23.45. On RxR-English val-unseen it gets SR 68.2 / nDTW 67.1 vs VLN-PETL 57.9 / 64.9, and on SOON test-unseen SR 40.50 / SPL 25.18 vs GridMM 36.27 / 21.25. The causal modules add about +2.5 SR / +3.4 SPL over the same model without interventions on R2R val-unseen.
limitations: Struggles with numerical references (e.g., 'the 5th chair') and with ambiguous instructions where multiple rooms fit the description.

The causal adjustments are heuristic deep-learning approximations (linear/attention-based expectations, K-means-sampled dictionaries). Different modalities prefer different estimators (statistic for vision, attention for text) without a principled explanation.

Gains are entangled with a strong base setup (CLIP features, METER init, augmented data, EnvEdit, speaker pseudo-labels): the no-intervention baseline already matches prior SOTA. Dictionary refresh is partly triggered by best val-unseen performance, so val-unseen numbers are not fully clean. Evaluation is only in discrete Matterport3D, with no continuous or real-robot evaluation.
